title: Naturality of the explicit Alexander--Whitney map
statement: Let X be a scheme with an additive monoidal tensor structure on its module sheaves. Let A,B,C,A1,B1,C1 be cosimplicial module sheaves, with pointwise tensor morphisms mu:A tensor B to C and mu1:A1 tensor B1 to C1, and cosimplicial maps f:A to A1, g:B to B1, k:C to C1. Suppose mu_n followed by k_n equals tensorHom(f_n,g_n) followed by mu1_n in every cosimplicial degree. Extend their alternating coface complexes by zero to integer degrees [lem-sc-module-cup-godement-cosimplicial-input]. There exist two Alexander--Whitney tensor cochain maps t and t1 whose (0,0) summands are the induced zero-degree pairings and such that t followed by the extended cochain map of k equals tensorHom of the extended maps of f and g followed by t1. No exactness, flasqueness, augmentation or Godement-model hypothesis is required.

source.place: §1.1.4, printed p. 16: front/back inclusions and formula immediately before (1.1.2).

proof.text: Use the explicit front/back summands and their coproduct descent for both pairings. Apply Mathlib HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor.d_eq, ι_D₁, ι_D₂, d₁_eq and d₂_eq directly in the cochain-map proof, simplify the two signs, and use the signed Leibniz identity. This gives cochain maps with exactly these components; negative-degree summands have a zero factor. No duplicate tensor differential helper is declared.

On a nonnegative bidegree, write the extended coefficient maps using extendMap_f. Cancel the extension identifications. Naturality of f and g moves their components across the front and back simplex inclusions. Apply the assumed square for the pointwise pairings. This proves naturality on each tensor summand; the coproduct hom_ext gives equality of cochain maps. The zero-zero summand formula gives both displayed equations.

lean.statement:
theorem moduleCup_cosimplicial_aw_natural (X : Scheme.{u})
    [MonoidalPreadditive X.Modules]
    (A B C A₁ B₁ C₁ : CosimplicialObject X.Modules)
    (μ : moduleCup_cosimplicialTensor X A B ⟶ C)
    (μ₁ : moduleCup_cosimplicialTensor X A₁ B₁ ⟶ C₁)
    (f : A ⟶ A₁) (g : B ⟶ B₁) (k : C ⟶ C₁)
    (hμ : ∀ n : SimplexCategory,
      μ.app n ≫ k.app n = (f.app n ⊗ₘ g.app n) ≫ μ₁.app n) :
    ∃ (t : HomologicalComplex.tensorObj (moduleCup_cosimplicialComplex X A)
        (moduleCup_cosimplicialComplex X B) ⟶ moduleCup_cosimplicialComplex X C)
      (t₁ : HomologicalComplex.tensorObj (moduleCup_cosimplicialComplex X A₁)
        (moduleCup_cosimplicialComplex X B₁) ⟶ moduleCup_cosimplicialComplex X C₁),
      HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj (moduleCup_cosimplicialComplex X A)
          (moduleCup_cosimplicialComplex X B) 0 0 0 (by simp) ≫ t.f 0 =
        moduleCup_cosimplicialZeroPair X A B C μ ∧
      HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj (moduleCup_cosimplicialComplex X A₁)
          (moduleCup_cosimplicialComplex X B₁) 0 0 0 (by simp) ≫ t₁.f 0 =
        moduleCup_cosimplicialZeroPair X A₁ B₁ C₁ μ₁ ∧
      t ≫ moduleCup_cosimplicialMap X k =
        HomologicalComplex.tensorHom (moduleCup_cosimplicialMap X f)
          (moduleCup_cosimplicialMap X g) ≫ t₁
